newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA BEATEN IN TEST WARM-UP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BEATEN IN TEST WARM-UP.

text.p: South African province Natal comfortably beat India by 52 runs at Kingsmead on Monday in a one-day match which the touring team preferred to treat as a practice game ahead of the second test starting in Cape Town on Thursday.
Natal's batsmen, boosted by a brilliant 63 not out from all-rounder Derek Crookes, effectively batted their opponents right out of the match with an imposing 288 for five in their 55 overs.
Left-handed opener Neil Johnson made an aggressive 80 and number three Errol Stewart a confident 64.

Of the Indian bowlers, only seamer Doda Ganesh commanded any measure of respect with his high action and ability to generate bounce. His one for 58 in 14 overs will probably earn him a first test cap at Newlands at the expense of fellow seamer Davd Johnson.
In reply, India could only reach 236 for seven, with number three Rahul Dravid being top scorer with a fluent 64 and left-hander Woorkeri Raman making a patient 54.
Although Dravid and Raman shared in a second-wicket stand of 101 in 23 overs, the rest of the Indian innings fell away as the asking rate climbed.
"They were under pressure right from the start of their innings to score a lot runs but they were also under pressure to bat for a long time," Natal captain Dale Benkenstein said.
"This led to some confusion in their team strategy as a result. Yet both sides were in need of match practice and, to that extent, this game was successful for both sides."
